nodes.description: Scope the assessment: which customer/project, which industry (steel, cement, chemicals, construction, energy), and which regulations are in scope (ets, cbam, csrd, fit-for-55, eu-ai-act). Matches the `/compliance-check` input contract.

Gather the agent's required inputs: annualEmissions, importValue, and the currentMeasures booleans (carbonReporting, emissionsMonitoring, supplyChainDueDiligence, aiSystemLogging). This is the node the existing multi-agent DAG has no explicit state for — inputs are assumed present today.

One or more required inputs is absent, stale, or implausible. This is the recovery path the `/workflow compliance-assessment` DAG does not model: decide whether to pull the value from a connected ERP/IoT source, ask the customer, or proceed on a flagged default. A default used here MUST be recorded so the final report can disclose it — never silently substituted.
First stage of the existing pipeline: emissions analysis. Produces the activity/verified emissions baseline the regulatory stage scores against.
Second stage: score current measures against each in-scope regulation's thresholds via `/compliance-check` (cli: `run compliance --input`). Produces per-regulation gaps and deadline urgency.

Compliance score below 50% — the `/compliance-check` skill's own documented threshold for escalating to the full assessment workflow. Flag deadline-critical gaps before continuing; a sub-50 score is a finding in its own right, not just a lower number.
Third stage: viability — can the identified gaps realistically be closed before their deadlines, at what cost. Completes the emissions -> regulatory -> viability pipeline.

Assemble the assessment: per-regulation gaps, deadline urgency, recommendations, and an explicit list of any flagged defaults used (from MISSING_DATA). Read-only deliverable — this graph produces an assessment, it does not file anything with a regulator, so no RED-zone gate applies here.
Terminal for this run — assessment abandoned (inputs unobtainable, customer deprioritized, or scope withdrawn). Re-enterable on the next cycle.
Terminal — assessment delivered. Feeds the MGD/CRC north-star (/mgd-report) as governed decisions.
